# Scott Christensen

> IT support technician — CompTIA A+ in progress

IT support technician with hands-on computer repair experience since 2010, utility field-safety experience, and a record of building, testing and running software on a self-managed Linux server. A problem solver who documents every fix so it is solved once. Currently studying for CompTIA A+.

Location: Fortuna, CA — open to relocation
Contact: scott@scottchristensen.dev

## Projects
- ProReady: Study platform for certification exams — multi-subject course packs, spaced-repetition review (FSRS), instructor review queue, encrypted content storage, and a full CompTIA A+ course. Built with Claude under my direction.
- Home server: Linux Mint server running my apps, Docker services, local AI models and document archiving.
- Hermes: Self-hosted platform of AI-assisted tools (website, image and app-building studios, a phone companion app, a job-search hub) running on my own Linux server. Built with Claude under my direction.
- Automated trading system (personal): Self-hosted system that monitors and manages my brokerage and crypto accounts with daily caps, kill switches and shadow-first rollouts. Built with Claude under my direction.
- Omnibus: Android audiobook player (Kotlin) with a Python + SQLite sync server on my home server — per-device tokens, private-network only, nightly backups kept 14 days; overnight transcription for read-along and spoiler-safe story help with a local AI model. Built with Claude under my direction.
- Epochron: Android calendar (Kotlin/Compose) with labels, sky events, weather and tides (NWS/NOAA), a trip card and tasks; one network door closed until weather is turned on; city-level location only. Built with Claude under my direction.
- HIL + Tabula Friends Edition: Offline screenshot/recording bar and project notepad packaged as a Windows installer and a Linux .deb. Built with Claude under my direction.
- App Ladder: Small utilities built for Linux, Windows and Android — Pulse (server health light), Drop (file send with revocable per-device tokens), Tally (shared lists on one shared sync service), Bell (push notifications without Google, in progress). Built with Claude under my direction.
- Iris: Android companion app (Capacitor) for my home server — voice notes, photos, GPS trip logging with mileage CSV export, and phone screen recording — connected over HTTPS on a private network. Built with Claude under my direction.
